steps.body: People hire people, not skill lists. In 60 seconds — a pitch, an "about" page, the start of a call — a client decides whether you feel *real and reliable*. Your story is genuinely good: sales supervisor for three years, now a data science student building real skill. That's not a weakness to hide; it's a narrative of someone who understands business AND data. This module turns that story into assets: your introduction, your 60-second pitch, your LinkedIn.

steps.heading: The branding rule
steps.body: every line must pass the honesty contract. "Skilled learner with real projects" beats "expert" every time — because it's true, and truth survives follow-up questions.

A good professional story has 3 beats. Here's yours — fill in the brackets honestly:

1. **Where you were:** *"I spent three years as a sales supervisor (2021–2024). I learned how businesses actually run — targets, customers, messy real-world data."*
2. **The turn:** *"In 2024 I started a BS in Data Science because I wanted to work with data, not just report it."*
3. **Where you are now:** *"I'm in my 5th semester, building real projects — [your actual project]. I help [who] with [specific problem] through [concrete deliverable]."*

Notice what's missing: no "passionate ninja guru," no fake years, no "I can do everything." Specificity IS the confidence.

steps.heading: Roman Urdu check
steps.body: *agar tum ye kahani apne dost ko suna sako bina sharmaye, to ye tayyar hai.* If you can tell this story to a friend without embarrassment, it's ready.

steps.title: Self-intro model (audio)
steps.tip: Steal the structure, keep your own facts.

steps.prompt:
**Record your pitch**

Write your 60-second pitch using the Hook → Proof → Offer structure. Record it. Listen back with this checklist: under 70 seconds? Falling intonation? Zero banned phrases? Clean ending (not trailing off)? Re-record twice. This recording is an asset — you'll reuse it for months.

steps.body: 60 seconds = ~130–150 words. Structure: **Hook (who you help) → Proof (one real thing) → Offer (what you do next).**

steps.heading: Model (adapt, don't copy)
steps.body: Delivery notes: 60 seconds, steady pace, falling intonation on statements (Module 3), pause after the proof (let it land), end with the offer — always end with a next step.
steps.example: "I'm Tanqeel, a data science student specializing in sales data analysis. I spent three years in sales before starting my degree, so I understand the business side — not just the code. Recently I built a sales dashboard analyzing 6,000 retail orders — I can show you the demo. I help small shops turn messy Excel files into clear monthly reports. If that's useful, I can look at a sample of your data, free, and tell you exactly what's possible."

steps.prompt:
**Build your LinkedIn**

Write: (1) your headline using the formula, (2) your 4-paragraph about section. Every claim must be verifiable — if you can't show it, cut it. Read it aloud: does it sound like you on your best day? That's the target.

steps.wrong: I am a highly skilled data scientist with many years of experience." → ?
steps.answer: I'm a data science student (5th semester) specializing in sales data analysis.
steps.hint: Read it aloud — where does it stumble?

steps.heading: Headline formula
steps.body:
[What you do] | [Who you help] | [Proof in 5 words]
*Example: "Data Science Student | Helping small shops turn Excel chaos into clear reports | Built a 6,000-order sales dashboard"*

steps.heading: About section (4 short paragraphs)
steps.body:
1. What you do and who it's for (2 lines).
2. Your background in one honest arc (the 3 beats, compressed).
3. One real proof with a number (project, orders analyzed, course completed).
4. Call to action: what to do next (DM me / see my work at [link]).

**Banned phrases** (they mark you as fake instantly): *"highly skilled," "years of experience" (you don't have them), "expert," "guru," "I can do any work," "cheap rates," "sir please give me a chance."* Confidence without begging: state the offer, state the next step, stop.

steps.heading: Headline
steps.body: Data Science Student | Helping small shops turn Excel chaos into clear sales reports | Built a 6,000-order retail dashboard

steps.heading: About
steps.body: Notice: every claim is checkable. No "expert," no "years of experience," no "cheap rates." The offer is specific and low-risk. That's what makes it strong.
steps.example:
I help small shop owners stop building sales reports by hand.
I spent three years as a sales supervisor (2021–2024), so I know how business decisions actually get made. In 2024 I started a BS in Data Science to work with data properly — I'm now in my 5th semester, building real projects in Python and data analysis.
Recent work: a sales dashboard analyzing 6,000 retail orders — cleaning messy Excel data, building clear charts, and delivering it as a link anyone can open. Happy to share the demo.
If your sales data lives in Excel and your monthly report eats a day of your life, message me. I'll look at a sample of your data, free, and tell you exactly what's possible.

steps.wrong: I can do any work you give me at very cheap rates." → ?
steps.answer: I build [specific deliverable] at fixed, fair prices — here's what $X gets you.
steps.hint: Read it aloud — where does it stumble?

steps.wrong: Please give me a chance sir, I will do my best." → ?
steps.answer: Cut entirely — replace with an offer: "Want me to look at a sample of your data, free?
steps.hint: Read it aloud — where does it stumble?

steps.wrong: I am expert in Python, ML, AI, deep learning etc." → ?
steps.answer: I'm building strong foundations in Python and data analysis — here's a project that shows where I am: [link].
steps.hint: Read it aloud — where does it stumble?

steps.title: "Tell me about yourself"
steps.prompt: AI tutor plays an interviewer. You get 90 seconds, then follow-up questions ("Why freelancing?" "What's your biggest strength?" "Where are you weakest?" — answer the weakness one HONESTLY: "I'm still building [X] — here's how I'm closing that gap."). Honesty about weakness, stated calmly, reads as strength.
steps.tip: Fluency mode: no stopping, no mid-sentence correcting.

steps.rule: 8/10 to move on. Answer first, then learn from the misses.

steps.heading: Can-do statements
steps.body:
- [ ] I can tell my 3-beat story in 60 seconds without notes
- [ ] My pitch has a hook, one real proof, and a clear next step
- [ ] My LinkedIn headline + about section are written, honest, and specific
- [ ] I can answer "tell me about yourself" and "what's your weakness" without inventing anything

steps.heading: Mini-test
steps.body: Send your pitch recording + LinkedIn about text to your AI tutor. One question: "Does anything here sound fake or vague?" Fix whatever it flags.

steps.heading: Re-entry note
steps.body:
Your pitch is a living asset. Re-record it monthly — it should get shorter and more specific as your real proof grows.
